newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PacDun in Telectronics sale talks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PacDun in Telectronics sale talks.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Friday it was in advanced negotiations for the sale of its troubled U.S. unit, Telectronics Pacing Systems.
"We are in very advanced negotations," Pacific Dunlop chairman John Gough told reporters.
Managing Director Rod Chadwick told reporters: "It's my expectations that we could do it within six months."
Chadwick said the company had provided A$91 million in its 1995/96 results for the expected loss on the sale of Telectronics.
Pacific Dunlop said abnormal losses of A$296 million after tax for the year included a A$340 million loss in respect of Telectronics.
There was an abnormal gain of A$44 million in respect of items other than Telectronics.

"The abnormal loss in respect of Telectronics comprises losses incurred during the year whilst manufacture for the U.S. market was under suspension pursuant to a consent decree with U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and an additional provision for ongoing patient care and monitoring, as well as provisions for an anticipated loss on disposal of the business," it said.
"Telectronics is presently engaged in advanced discussions with several parties regarding the sale of the business," Pacific Dunlop said in its profit statement.
Earlier Pacific Dunlop reported a net loss of A$132.74 million for 1995/96, versus 1994/95's A$94.2 million net profit.
This included abnormal losses before tax of A$284.55 million, compared with an abnormal loss of A$197.28 million the previous year.

"The depth of the Telectronics losses coming on top of a generally poorer trading performance and increased margins pressure has required a major restructuring of the company," Pacific Dunlop Chairman John Gough said in a statement.
The sale of Telectronics and the completed sale of Cochlear meant Pacific Dunlop had completed the withdrawal from the manufacturing and sale of implantable medical products.
Pacific Dunlop set a final dividend of three cents.
Telectronics had losses from its operating activities totalling A$164 million in 1995/96, with A$90 million of losses in the second half and A$74 million in the first half.
"The loss includes A$10 million in restructuring expenses as Telectronics reduced its employee numbers by approximately 200 and closed a number of operations," it said.
The losses were incurred while manufacturing was suspended, but approval for a resumption to manufacturing was granted on June 20, 1996.

Telectronics' abnormal losses include a provision of A$85 million for the costs of the Accufix Research Institute established shortly after the recall of Accufix's pacemaker leads and A$91 million for anticipated losses linked to the disposal of Telectronics.
Pacific Dunlop said Telectronics continued to vigourously defend all law suits and no provision had been made for any payouts arising from litigation except legal costs.
Pacific Dunlop's shares were up seven cents at A$2.72 at 3.30 pm (0530 GMT).
